name: Osun Printed Banded-Collar Shirt
description:
A short-sleeve button-front shirt with a banded (mandarin) collar and a West African-inspired geometric print — deep indigo and burnt sienna on a cream ground, with a repeating angular motif that references Yoruba textile traditions while feeling entirely contemporary. Made by Osun Workshop, a small-batch label run out of a Tier 3 residential block in the Chicago south corridor by a second-generation textile designer. The fabric is a medium-weight linen-cotton blend that breathes in humid summers and holds its shape after hand washing.

Each run of prints is different — Osun releases maybe four patterns a year, and once they're gone, they're gone. The shirts have become a quiet status marker in certain creative and professional circles: not flashy, but specific. You either know Osun or you don't.
what_it_says: You have taste that runs deeper than a corporate catalog, and you support independent makers when you can afford to.
story_hooks: A specific Osun print — a limited run of 40 shirts — was worn by several attendees at a protest that turned violent. The print has since become associated with the event, and wearing it now carries unintended political weight.
The designer behind Osun has received a buyout offer from a Tier 4 corponation that wants to scale the brand. Regulars are watching to see if she takes it.

A fake Osun shirt has appeared on the market — close enough to fool most people, but the print is slightly wrong in a way that experts can spot. Someone is trying to understand who's buying the real ones.

physical_description.visual_profile: A refined, culturally-rooted casual shirt with understated presence. The banded mandarin collar sits crisp against the neck, framing the face with geometric precision. Short sleeves hit mid-bicep with a relaxed but intentional cut. The overall silhouette reads approachable yet distinctive—neither oversized nor fitted, but confident in its own geometry.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed-tailored; structured enough to hold shape when untucked, but not constraining. Designed for layering or solo wear. Sits naturally across the shoulders with slight ease through the torso.
physical_description.primary_material: Linen-cotton blend (medium-weight); breathable, naturally textured weave that softens with wear and washing
physical_description.texture: Subtly slubbed surface with a lived-in hand; slightly crisp fresh from washing, softening to a gentle drape after a few wears. The print sits flat on the fabric with clean registration.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep indigo and burnt sienna geometric motifs on a cream ground. Angular repeating pattern inspired by Yoruba textile traditions—sharp lines, interlocking forms, warm-cool contrast that reads modern despite its cultural reference.
physical_description.closures: Mother-of-pearl button front; four buttons spaced evenly down the front placket
distinctive_features: Hand-screen-printed West African geometric pattern (limited batch)
Each production run features unique colorway/motif variation
Reinforced seams at stress points; finished interior with topstitching
Subtle Osun Workshop label at left chest or interior neckline
Pattern registration precision signals artisanal but intentional production
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 aspirational to Tier 2 selective—affordable craft luxury, not mass-produced, not accessible to every consumer
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer signals: cultural literacy, support for independent makers, creative professional identity, appreciation for non-Western design heritage applied with contemporary sensibility. Suggests someone in arts, design, creative tech, or thoughtful corpo work. Coded as 'in the know' within GLMZ creative circles.
physical_description.condition_typical: Crisp and structured when new; breaks in beautifully with gentle wear and hand washing. Shows soft creasing at collar and sleeve folds, slight fading in the cream ground with age—wear enhances rather than diminishes the shirt's appeal.
